correctness.rationale: The published finite map \((\mathbb P^n)^d\to\operatorname{Split}_d(\mathbb P^n)\) has degree \(d!\) and pulls the hyperplane class back to \(H_1+\cdots+H_d\), so top intersection gives \(\deg=(nd)!/(d!(n!)^d)\). The map factors through the symmetric product, and unique factorization makes the induced finite map bijective on complex points; compact-to-Hausdorff then gives a homeomorphism. The Macdonald identity yields \(\chi=\binom{n+d}{d}\). The two displayed adjacent-parameter ratios are strictly greater than one for \(n,d\ge2\), and the three base values settle every case. The package checker independently verifies the formulas and ratios through a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: The split-form Chow variety is a canonical projective model for completely factored homogeneous polynomials and underlies Chow rank and symmetric tensor-decomposition questions. Projective degree measures a generic complementary linear intersection, while Euler characteristic measures the topology of the underlying symmetric product. The theorem gives a complete two-parameter phase diagram between these canonical complexities, with a single nontrivial equality at reducible quadrics in four variables. The exact coordinate-growth law explains the transition structurally rather than by finite casework.
